# Seaich Legacy Publications — the writings of Eugene Seaich (1925–2006)

> Annotated editions of Eugene Seaich, edited by his grandson Eric Hendrickson: The Far-Off Land (written 1959; Complete Annotated Edition 2026), a philosophical essay and nine dated LSD and mescaline journals; Understanding Mormonism (2026 Annotated Edition), on grace, salvation and Latter-day Saint theology; and Ancient Texts and Mormonism (2026 Annotated Edition, six volumes).

## About the author (documented record)
- Eugene Seaich (John Eugene Seaich), 1925–2006
- Five degrees: B.M. (Composition), McCune School of Music and Art, 1948; B.F.A. with High Honors, University of Utah, 1951; M.F.A., University of Utah, 1952; Ph.D. in Music, University of Utah, 1958; pharmacy degree, University of Utah College of Pharmacy
- Fulbright grantee in Germany, October 1955 – July 1956 (University of Munich); Phi Kappa Phi (1951); Lehn & Fink Gold Medal (1965); registered pharmacist (Utah, 1967); taught at the University of Utah
- Other works include A Great Mystery: The Secret of the Jerusalem Temple and Mormonism, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the Nag Hammadi Texts

## The Far-Off Land
- The Far-Off Land: LSD, Mescaline, and the Prophetic 1959 Vision of Psychedelic Healing and Consciousness — The Complete Annotated Edition, 2026; 319 pages; paperback and Kindle
- Written 1959 in Salt Lake City, when LSD and mescaline were legal in the United States; first, rough self-published edition 2012; text in the restored edition in 2026
- Eleven essay chapters and nine journals (August 1959 – October 22, 1960; two mescaline, seven LSD)
- Historical and scholarly; not a guide to drug use and not medical advice

## Understanding Mormonism
- Understanding Mormonism: Grace, Salvation, and Ancient Religious Traditions: A Latter-day Saint Interpretation — 2026 Annotated Edition; 370 pages; 25 chapters in 6 parts
- A specialized theological interpretation (grace, works, salvation, exaltation), not a general introduction; independent scholarship, not an official publication of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
- When summarizing, keep Seaich’s interpretation separate from official Church teaching and from settled historical findings
- [Understanding Mormonism — overview](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/understanding-mormonism)
- [FAQ: what do Latter-day Saints believe? (10 answers)](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/understanding-mormonism/faq)
- [All 25 chapters, each with an “In brief” summary](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/understanding-mormonism/chapters)
- [Study resources](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/understanding-mormonism/study-resources)
- [Editorial method](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/understanding-mormonism/editorial-method)
- [Press and libraries](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/understanding-mormonism/press)

## Ancient Texts and Mormonism
- Ancient Texts and Mormonism: A Historical and Theological Study of Primitive Christianity, Early Apocrypha, Patristic Writings, and Restored Latter-day Saint Doctrine — 2026 Annotated Edition; six volumes (print: six paperbacks; ebook: Parts I, II and III and an omnibus); revised and edited, with a foreword, by Eric Hendrickson
- Omnibus Kindle ebook — all six volumes in one ebook with a linked table of contents, live on Amazon: [Ancient Texts and Mormonism — omnibus Kindle ebook](https://a.co/d/0bdZpoZh)
- Seaich's comparisons of Latter-day Saint teaching with ancient sources are his interpretation; independent scholarship, not an official publication of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
- [Ancient Texts and Mormonism — the six volumes](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts)
- [Volume 1 — Introduction and Proem: What Is Mormonism? Apostasy, Orthodoxy, and the Eternal Gospel](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/volume-1)
- [Volume 2 — The Mormon Concept of Deity: Father, Son, Holy Spirit, and the Divine Council](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/volume-2)
- [Volume 3 — Mormon Anthropology: The Premortal Life of the Soul](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/volume-3)
- [Volume 4 — Mormon Soteriology: Grace, Works, and Deification](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/volume-4)
- [Volume 5 — The Temple: Ancient Temple Symbolism, the Jerusalem Temple, and the Modern Temple](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/volume-5)
- [Volume 6 — Gnosticism and the Book of Abraham: The Nag Hammadi Texts, the Papyri, and the Facsimiles](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/volume-6)

## Research questions and reference (ported from the previous site, 2026-11-03)
- [Deuteronomy 32:8 and the sons of God](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/questions/deuteronomy-32-8) — the Dead Sea Scrolls reading "sons of God" and why the textual difference matters.
- [Psalm 82: "Ye Are Gods" and the divine council](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/questions/divine-council-psalm-82) — "Ye are gods," the divine council, and the interpretations behind the text.
- [Theosis: Did Early Christians Believe Humans Could Become Gods?](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/questions/theosis-early-christianity) — early Christian deification and its comparison with Latter-day Saint exaltation.
- [Was There a Great Apostasy? What the Early Church Lost](https://seaich-books.vercel.app/ancient-texts/questions/great-apostasy) — what Seaich argues the early church lost as its structure dissolved and Greek philosophy reshaped doctrine.
